why: A `killedBy` entry whose named test PASSED under the mutation must mismatch by name -- that rot is the one thing the named-test contract exists to catch; treating every name as satisfied turns killedBy into an outcome-only pin.
killedBy: end-to-end: real apply -> real vitest subprocess -> real restore a real killedBy entry matches when its named test fails, and a name that does not fail is a mismatch that names it (issue #504)
killedBy: the verdict through fake deps mismatches, naming the test, when the named test passed while others failed -- the rot case; the count-only entry is the negative control
